_comment: Words ignored when deciding whether two titles share a term.
This is the one list on the site that is ours rather than Clarivate's, and it
is kept here in the open so it can be argued with. Everything else that groups
or filters a paper comes from Web of Science; this only decides which lines get
drawn between papers that are already placed.
"applied" names the lists actually in force. Only ordinary English function
words are applied: the, of, with. Everything else in a title counts, including
words that look like research boilerplate.
The boilerplate list below is kept and NOT applied. It was written on the
assumption that words like research, review and article say nothing about
subject matter, which is wrong in this lab: peer review is the subject of the
Matthew effect paper, and research methods is the subject of the team science
review. Rather than sort the honest cases from the dishonest ones word by word,
nothing but function words is dropped. Add "boilerplate" to "applied" to put
Matching is on lightly stemmed words, so network/networks and study/studies
collapse together and only one form needs listing.
